datasetName: Sea Watch Foundation Marine Megafauna Sightings: 1971 to present
fieldNotes: Very large baleen whale (I am quite used to Minkes) ca 1 km offshore. Seen to breathe twice and then dive before being picked up again ca 5 to 10 mins later where it was again observed to breath twice before diving.  High dorsal fin strongly recurved (ie curved backwards). Head appeared first. then a pause or gap before back and fin. Back and fin semed to come high out of water especially on dive roll.  So much so that on first observation I thought that there were two animals.  No blow seen (too distant and colour of sea light grey).  Moving steadily south.  Clearly one of the two bigger baleen whales (if blue ruled out).  Film on this website suggests to me strongly that it is Sei rather than Fin. I have seen many Fin whales in Bay of Biscay but that was a few years ago now and the angle of view was different. This animal 'felt' different somehow
